proposal.comment: [Playbook] We accept the IP indemnity but cannot live with a 10-day notice condition; notice should be prompt with a materiality/prejudice qualifier. We have also added the standard indemnity for Garman's breach of law, misconduct and data incidents.

ops.newText: Garman shall also defend, indemnify and hold harmless Sparkling and its affiliates against any third-party claim to the extent arising out of Garman's breach of applicable law, its gross negligence or wilful misconduct, or any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Sparkling's data caused by Garman. Sparkling shall notify Garman in writing promptly after a responsible officer of Sparkling becomes aware of any such claim, provided that any failure or delay in giving such notice shall not relieve Garman of its obligations except to the extent Garman is materially prejudiced thereby.
ops.oldText: Sparkling shall notify Garman in writing of any such claim within ten calendar days of a responsible officer of Sparkling becoming aware of such claim.

proposal.summary: A Vendor IP indemnity is present with the usual procure/modify/replace remedies, which meets our fallback. Two points to fix: the ten-calendar-day notice condition is a trap (notice should be prompt and failure should only matter if it prejudices Garman), and there is no express duty to defend or indemnity for Garman's breach of law, gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

quote: Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless from any and all losses, damages and expenses including without limitation, court costs, arbitration fees, penalties, fines, amounts paid in settlement of claims and reasonable legal fees and expenses of investigation (collectively the "Losses") which Sparkling or any of its respective officers or directors may incur due to a breach of this warranty. Sparkling shall notify Garman in writing of any such claim within ten calendar days of a responsible officer of Sparkling becoming aware of such claim.
rationale: A Vendor IP indemnity is present with the usual procure/modify/replace remedies, which meets our fallback. Two points to fix: the ten-calendar-day notice condition is a trap (notice should be prompt and failure should only matter if it prejudices Garman), and there is no express duty to defend or indemnity for Garman's breach of law, gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own custom Modifications we commission and pay for, or at minimum hold a perpetual, irrevocable licence to them, and our data remains ours. Garman's ownership of its underlying platform is unaffected.

ops.newText: No title to Garman's pre-existing intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement. Sparkling shall own all right, title and interest in the Modifications and any other deliverables developed specifically for Sparkling and paid for by Sparkling, and Garman hereby assigns the same to Sparkling; to the extent any Garman intellectual property is embedded therein, Garman grants Sparkling a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense it for Sparkling's business purposes. Sparkling retains all right, title and interest in and to all data and content of Sparkling processed using the Software, and Garman acquires no rights therein.
ops.oldText: No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement.

proposal.summary: Garman keeping its platform is fine, but it also takes ownership of the Modifications built to our Specifications and paid for by us, and there is no provision confirming that Sparkling retains all rights in its own data processed with the Software. We own what we pay for and everything we put in.

quote: Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto), including all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement.
rationale: Garman keeping its platform is fine, but it also takes ownership of the Modifications built to our Specifications and paid for by us, and there is no provision confirming that Sparkling retains all rights in its own data processed with the Software. We own what we pay for and everything we put in.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that indemnities, confidentiality, data/security breaches, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud sit outside any liability limitation. We have kept Section 15 mutual and have not asked for a monetary cap; we only expanded the carve-out sentence.

ops.newText: The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14, to either party's indemnification obligations, to a party's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, or to any unauthorized access to, use or disclosure of the other party's data or Confidential Information.
ops.oldText: The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14.

proposal.summary: Section 15 is mutual and contains no monetary cap, which we are content to leave as-is (no cap on Garman's exposure). The gap is the carve-out list: only Sections 13 (IP) and 14 (confidentiality) sit outside the limitation, so indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and data/security breaches are otherwise squeezed into "direct damages" only. We propose adding the standard carve-outs.

quote: The exclusive remedy of either party in a claim against the other under this Agreement shall be the recovery of its direct damages. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages
rationale: Section 15 is mutual and contains no monetary cap, which we are content to leave as-is (no cap on Garman's exposure). The gap is the carve-out list: only Sections 13 (IP) and 14 (confidentiality) sit outside the limitation, so indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and data/security breaches are otherwise squeezed into "direct damages" only. We propose adding the standard carve-outs.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept an assignment bar without an affiliate/successor carve-out, and consent for other assignments should not be unreasonably withheld. Section 3(c) should be conformed.

ops.newText: Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed; provided that Sparkling may assign this Agreement, without consent, to an affiliate or to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, corporate reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets.
ops.oldText: Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.

proposal.summary: A blanket consent requirement with no reasonableness standard and no affiliate or M&A carve-out for Sparkling is a walk-away for us; Section 3(c) reinforces the same prohibition. We need the freedom to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a corporate transaction.

quote: Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
rationale: A blanket consent requirement with no reasonableness standard and no affiliate or M&A carve-out for Sparkling is a walk-away for us; Section 3(c) reinforces the same prohibition. We need the freedom to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a corporate transaction.

quote: a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use
rationale: No exclusivity, sole-supplier or requirements obligation is imposed on Sparkling; we remain free to procure alternatives.

quote: Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
rationale: No liquidated damages, penalties or early-termination fee is payable by Sparkling on termination.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The licence must extend to contractors acting for us and must transfer to a successor in a corporate transaction; otherwise routine M&A would break the licence.

ops.newText: for the use of Sparkling, affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations and contractors acting on Sparkling's behalf, a non-exclusive licence, transferable to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of Sparkling's assets, to use
ops.oldText: for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use

proposal.summary: Affiliates are covered, but the licence excludes contractors acting on our behalf and is flatly non-transferable, so it would not survive a merger or reorganisation. Our fallback requires transferability to a successor in an M&A transaction.

quote: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use
rationale: Affiliates are covered, but the licence excludes contractors acting on our behalf and is flatly non-transferable, so it would not survive a merger or reorganisation. Our fallback requires transferability to a successor in an M&A transaction.

quote: not use the Work to act as a service bureau in whole or in part, for any other Person, except for any affiliate of Sparkling operating at the Authorized Locations
rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Sparkling's business; the only restriction is a customary service-bureau limit on use of Garman's software, which we accept.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; 60 days is our fallback. Please also conform the notice-period reference later in this subsection.

ops.newText: Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon thirty (30) calendar days written notice to Garman, in which case Garman shall refund any fees prepaid in respect of the period after the effective date of termination.
ops.oldText: Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.

proposal.summary: We have a convenience right (good, and Garman has none), but the notice period is 90 days and there is no refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period. Our position is 30 days with a pro-rata refund.

quote: Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
rationale: We have a convenience right (good, and Garman has none), but the notice period is 90 days and there is no refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period. Our position is 30 days with a pro-rata refund.

quote: provided that Sparkling may itself or by retaining independent experts, examine and test the materials for compliance with the obligations of Garman hereunder
rationale: No audit, inspection or verification right is granted to Garman over Sparkling's usage or systems; the only examination right runs in our favour.

quote: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
rationale: Nova Scotia law is outside our standard list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales), but it is Sparkling's own home jurisdiction (Dartmouth, NS) rather than the vendor's, and jurisdiction is non-exclusive with no foreign arbitration. We are comfortable accepting this as drafted unless business prefers otherwise.

quote: Sparkling shall pay the fees as set out in the Fee Schedule in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and the Fee Schedule.
rationale: No most-favoured-nation or price-matching obligation is imposed on Sparkling.

quote: Sparkling shall pay the fees as set out in the Fee Schedule in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and the Fee Schedule.
rationale: No minimum purchase or take-or-pay language appears in the body, but Schedule "A" (Fee Schedule) is not attached. We should review it for minimum commitments, shortfall charges and fees triggered by additional Authorized Locations before signing.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We can agree a mutual, 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, but not a no-hire binding our affiliates. We have added the standard general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.

ops.newText: both parties agree not to solicit for employment any employee of the other party who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement, provided that nothing in this Section shall restrict either party from hiring any person who responds to a general advertisement or other solicitation not specifically directed at the other party's personnel, or who approaches a party on an unsolicited basis
ops.oldText: both parties agree not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire any employee of the other party, or any person who was an employee of the other party during the previous six months and who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement

proposal.summary: This is a no-hire (not a non-solicit), it binds our affiliates, it appears to cover any Garman employee rather than only those involved in the services, and there is no carve-out for general advertising or unsolicited approaches. No-hire provisions are a walk-away for us.

quote: both parties agree not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire any employee of the other party, or any person who was an employee of the other party during the previous six months and who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement
rationale: This is a no-hire (not a non-solicit), it binds our affiliates, it appears to cover any Garman employee rather than only those involved in the services, and there is no carve-out for general advertising or unsolicited approaches. No-hire provisions are a walk-away for us.

quote: For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
rationale: Maintenance runs in "renewable" one-year terms but the renewal mechanics are undefined (no auto-renewal/non-renewal notice window) and there is no cap on maintenance fee increases on renewal. We should confirm the Fee Schedule caps any uplift (our position: lesser of CPI and 3%, fallback 5%).

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Exit needs to be symmetrical: we get transition help and our data back before anything is deleted. Our fallback is 90 days of assistance with data export within 30 days.

ops.newText: and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes. Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Garman shall (i) at Sparkling's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Garman's then-current rates; (ii) within thirty (30) calendar days, return to Sparkling all Sparkling data in its possession in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (iii) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.
ops.oldText: and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.

proposal.summary: Exit obligations run one way: we must cease use and return everything, with no transition assistance and no obligation on Garman to return or delete Sparkling data in its possession (e.g. from conversion and support work). Source-code escrow mitigates but does not replace this.

quote: Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
rationale: Exit obligations run one way: we must cease use and return everything, with no transition assistance and no obligation on Garman to return or delete Sparkling data in its possession (e.g. from conversion and support work). Source-code escrow mitigates but does not replace this.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

quote: For the acceptance period and for a period of one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and thereafter for as long as the Software is covered by Maintenance Services and is used by Sparkling in accordance with this Agreement, Garman warrants that the Software shall perform in conformance with the Specifications in all material respects.
rationale: A 12-month (and, while maintenance continues, ongoing) conformance warranty with a repair remedy under Section 10(c), and no general "AS IS" disclaimer, exceeds our preferred position. We would add a no-malicious-code and compliance-with-laws warranty if the negotiation allows, but this is not a blocker.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We ask vendors that touch our systems and data to carry standard CGL, E&O and cyber cover; our fallback is E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

ops.newText: (e) The parties are acting as independent contractors under this Agreement and not as agents or representatives of the other and not as partners or joint ventures. Garman shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Garman processes Sparkling data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Garman shall provide certificates of insurance on request.
